answer:
Verdict: expected seasonality. This is not an incident and I would not open one.

The monitor is correct that a threshold was crossed -- observed spend of $48,200 against a threshold of $30,000 on the monitor's summary view for account 419283746501. So the alert is not a false reading; the question is what it means.

The baseline is what settles it:

- June 2026: $48,200
- May 2026: $19,400
- June 2025: $45,700

Against last month this looks like a 2.5x jump. Against the same month a year earlier it is a 5% increase, which is ordinary growth. A pattern that repeats annually in the same month is seasonality, not an anomaly -- and the monitor's threshold is a flat monthly figure, so it will fire every June regardless.

The capacity manager rules out the other explanation. Overall utilisation is 97.7%, with only $1,100 of the $48,200 sitting in unused reservation. High spend on well-utilised capacity is workload, not waste -- if this were an incident, or a provisioning mistake, I would expect idle reserved capacity and a low utilisation figure.

The action here is not an incident but a threshold that does not model the annual cycle. Either raise the June threshold or make it relative to the same month last year, otherwise this alert will recur next June and cost someone the same investigation.
